title: Periodontal status and oral microbiota in association with general health status in patients in residential care facilities
summary:
Background: Demographic change and the associated ageing of German society are a key issue in current and future healthcare policy. Frequent multimorbidity, immobility, mental and cognitive problems and inadequate access to dental prevention, treatment and care impair needs-based dental health care for older (geriatric) patients. Inflammatory diseases of the periodontium in particular represent a risk factor for a large number of systemic diseases. In order to be able to regularly integrate adequate dental/periodontological treatment strategies into geriatric complex therapy, it is advisable to assess the periodontal status depending on the patient's general condition and care status. 
Material and method: The intraoral microbiome of 300 geriatric inpatients will be analysed in relation to general diseases and care status. Periodontal diagnostics will be performed according to the guidelines of the CDC (Centers of disease control and prevention) and the current classification of periodontal diseases. The intraoral plaque samples/patient are pooled and microbial DNA is isolated. Next generation sequencing (NGS) will be used to analyse the microbial metagenome. 
Expected results: We expect that intraoral dysbiosis associated with periodontal changes is associated with general diseases or with the level of care of geriatric patients.  We hypothesise that dentate patients show differences in the oral microbiota and in the severity of general diseases compared to edentulous patients.
Conclusion: This study will collect data on the periodontal health of older adults, which could help to develop recommendations for the implementation and improvement of dental care in geriatric care.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Geriatric inpatients and patients capable of giving consent 
- Age: ≥ 60 years
- No family relationship between the study participants
Exclusion criteria:
- Subgingival periodontal therapy within 6 months prior to sample collection
- Systemic antibiotic therapy within 3 months prior to sample collection
- Refusal to participate, inability to complete questionnaires
